changelog: PegaProx 1.3.0 - PegaProx itself becomes highly available: up to four instances form a group with one leader and warm standbys, next to automated Proxmox VE installations, bulk actions on guests, new alert sources, a second security pass after 1.2.0 and a fix for a silent data loss in the ESXi live clone migration. HA (#625): a second PegaProx can run as a warm standby of the first. It is paired once with a one-time code, pulls the shared configuration every 30 seconds, shows the clusters live and read only, and is promoted to leader by an admin when the leader is gone; the old leader steps aside as soon as it sees it was replaced, also when it comes back later. A group holds up to four instances: one leader that runs all automation and holds the configuration, up to two members the leader makes active to serve users (consoles, shells and SPICE open there, every change goes to the leader), and standbys that wait to take over. A standby hands a signed-in user's changes to the leader, which checks the account against its own users and names the standby in the audit log (on by default, switchable per instance). Members talk over calls signed with Ed25519 that are useless anywhere else or later, a removed member is refused everywhere and goes passive, and a sync never silently wipes what a member holds: whatever it would replace is kept as an encrypted copy an admin can download or dismiss, and a snapshot older than the member's configuration is refused. Schedules run in the group's time zone, and changing it moves the last-run stamps so nothing runs twice or is skipped. LDAP and OIDC sign-ins on a standby go by the synced account and write nothing there. All of it lives in a new High Availability tab in the settings, with a banner for every user on a standby, in all three layouts and all nine languages. Groundwork for automatic failover is included but not yet enabled. NODE RECOVERY: PegaProx's own node recovery moves a guest only when every volume it starts with is on shared storage, and reads a dead node's guest configs from the cluster file system on other nodes instead of guessing; a node that returns during its recovery keeps what is left and no guest runs twice; a recovery that could not finish is listed in the cluster's HA settings, where the guests whose config already moved can be started. A new self-fence agent (its own unit, pegaprox-fence-agent) decides by quorum first and asks PegaProx only where quorum cannot decide; an agent of the old kind stays as it is until it is installed again, and the HA settings show which one runs on each node. Two-node and forced-quorum clusters set up from now on are recovered only after a fence per node that was read back; existing setups keep their behaviour behind an explicit "unsafe two-node recovery" switch. NEW: automated Proxmox VE installations - PegaProx serves the answer file to the Proxmox installer, each profile with its own fetch token and every run tracked from the first fetch to the installer's post-installation webhook, with a six-step guided setup that hashes the root password on the server, an answer file editor that refuses what the installer would refuse, encrypted storage and a page of its own in all three layouts (autoinstall.view and autoinstall.manage, for accounts that see every cluster). Bulk actions on selected guests - start, shut down, stop, reboot, snapshot and tags - in every layout, each guest checked on its own and the result shown per guest; a node can start, stop or migrate all its guests at once. Favorites are stored again and show as a group at the top of the sidebar in Modern and Corporate. New alert sources: failed Proxmox tasks such as a failed vzdump, Ceph health, failing or lagging replication, a ZFS pool that is not ONLINE or shows errors, and snapshots older than a set age, each raised once with a resolved notice and mutable per rule or per object; rolling updates can alert when a run starts and finishes and when a node's reboot is handed over (#716). Bulk migration runs on the server one guest at a time, a few at once or all at once, follows each guest and can be cancelled, also across page reloads (#952). Guests that no backup job covers are listed in the All Clusters overview and can raise an alert, with a grace period for new guests and a no-backup tag for intentional gaps. Cloud can be picked as the layout at the first login. Containers can be created from OCI images on PVE 9.1 and newer, from a small catalog or any image reference (a technology preview, as in Proxmox). Rolling updates can move a node's templates with its guests (#763) and let negative affinity rules give way for the run, switched back on afterwards (#954), in scheduled runs and in a node's maintenance as well. ProxLB pin tags (plb_pin_) rank a drain's targets instead of blocking it, with switches for strict pins and an automatic move back in the cluster settings, which also list the guests off their pin and can move them back (#811). Directory mappings and virtiofs shares can be set up in the VM hardware settings, checked before they reach PVE, with a warning before a guest that uses one is migrated. The All Clusters overview lists the storage of every cluster and exports the guest inventory with vCPU, memory, disks, IPs, HA state, tags and pool. Node temperatures work without lm-sensors, read from the kernel's hwmon. A node's ZFS pools show their device tree with error counts and the last scrub. The VM hardware settings can add a VirtIO RNG, checked against what QEMU accepts before it reaches PVE. A Site Recovery test failover keeps a boot screenshot of every guest it started as evidence. The command palette finds guests by MAC address, IP and notes. Admins can show a broadcast banner to everyone or to chosen tenants and roles. Check connection runs read-only probes against a cluster (API and fallback hosts, TLS fingerprint, the token's privileges against what PegaProx needs, versions, clock, quorum, SSH) and names a fix for each failed item. Container features (nesting, keyctl, fuse, mknod, NFS/CIFS) can be changed after creation, and PCI and USB passthrough can use the cluster's resource mappings, which also work on API-token clusters. A metrics.view permission lets a Prometheus scrape run without an admin token (#818), and the exporter also reports storage use per storage, replication state and age per job, the age of each guest's newest backup and guest disk I/O. The HTTP API is described in OpenAPI, generated from the routes and naming the permission each one demands (#104, #693), and can be browsed inside PegaProx from the user menu. Also: a System theme that follows the OS (#743), plugins limited to chosen clusters (#642), PEGAPROX_CONFIG_DIR and PEGAPROX_LOG_DIR (#826), the QEMU description in the Corporate summary (#813), a per-cluster switch that turns SSH off entirely (#941), PBS servers that connect with an API token (#805), a Tools section in the Corporate sidebar, the ESXi infrastructure view in all nine languages, a refreshed cloud image catalog (Ubuntu 26.04, Debian 13, AlmaLinux and Rocky Linux 10, Fedora 44, Alpine 3.24) that passes the CPU model the EL images need, a release Docker image for 32-bit ARM, release images on Python 3.12.15, and snapshot .deb builds of the Testing branch (#973, #974). PERFORMANCE: answers on kept-alive connections no longer wait for a delayed ACK, about 2-3 ms instead of 45 ms per request; the cluster health check reads all storage in one call (#946). CONSOLE: the console behind a reverse proxy is fixed end to end - the API port is no longer replaced by the VNC port, the configured port is used where 8006 was hard-coded, the upgrade carries credentials that match the ticket, a websocket is no longer upgraded twice, a session no longer ends a tenth of a second after it opens and partial sends are completed (#945, #955, #956); clusters with only an API token open consoles (#955); an error left behind by another TLS connection no longer ends a healthy console (#713); Stable Mode keeps the frame order instead of closing with 4099 (#955); paste types the right characters on de, es, fr, it, pt, pl and en-gb keymaps (#959); the terminal follows the bind address (#957) and no longer writes its script to /tmp under a predictable name (#958); the node shell no longer lets Firefox pan the page sideways (#727). UPDATES: Check for updates refreshes apt on the nodes first, and a refresh that failed is reported as a failed check instead of stale packages shown as current; rolling updates reboot once instead of waiting out a reboot that already happened (#953), evacuate guests only to nodes they may run on under HA affinity rules and storage availability (#647), and read the debsecan urgency correctly (#827); the PBS update panel shows its lines again instead of [object Object] (#964, #971). SECURITY: a second pass after 1.2.0, over the remaining penetration test findings and the daily code scans, including defects in 1.2.0's own fixes. A delegate with admin.users could demote an administrator and replace their password in one request; read routes next to gated write routes handed out every tenant's custom roles, pool permissions, VM ACLs and the cluster security audit; an API token with a lower role than its account got its privileges back through VM ACLs, list routes and the cluster gate; a deleted VM's ACL went to the next guest on that VMID; the ESXi credential guard could be passed by leaving the password out or by disabling the server first; an iSCSI CHAP secret sat in the node's process table; replacing a second factor needed no password; storage.create was never enforced; the 1.2.0 syslog gate never worked on a locked database, validators accepted a trailing newline, and a rate-limit cap could reset the login limits; an ntfy topic URL reached the log in full and per-cluster log files still took forged lines; a logo URL could put script on the public status page; host key pins could be lost under concurrent writes; and caller-supplied list limits are bounded. The release images verify the packages they install as root. A third round, on the rest of the penetration test and the code scans of 5 and 6 October: the PVE console ticket goes only to PegaProx's own console server; an API token secret is never offered as an SSH password; a cluster edit can no longer send its stored credential to a new address or inject an SSH option; a tenant override bounds the admin it lowers; accounts limited to pools or guests make no root@pam change, write no shared storage content and place no guest; migration paths no longer pass credentials where others can read them, keep node files private and destroy only what they copied; guest routes ask the right permission and act as the right principal; installation-wide reads, the updater, drift baselines and schedules ask who may; host key pins survive unreadable files and races; slow or greedy clients no longer hold the request pool or the syslog queue; and the CI actions and images are pinned, static downloads verified and PyJWT kept at 2.15.1 or newer (#972). BEHAVIOUR CHANGES: thirty-eight, listed in the update dialog. Several take something away from an existing setup: adding storage needs storage.create, a deleted custom role grants nothing instead of the viewer set, a user whose directory group holds a pool grant is now confined to that pool, node recovery leaves a guest with a local volume where it is (a local ISO included), and the cloud image ids fedora-40, debian-11 and alpine-319 are gone. Please read them before updating a multi-tenant install or one that uses PegaProx node recovery. FIXES: the ESXi live clone migration (Live Clone and Auto) lost every write made on the source after its snapshot, during the copy and during the confirmation hold (#1124); the switchover now stops the source, folds the snapshot back, compares every block and copies what changed, runs the post-copy steps only then and powers the source back on if anything fails before the target runs, so it takes longer than the few seconds it used to; the block delta of the pre-sync migration copied only the head of each changed block and still reported success, changed blocks now arrive whole and are read back; Windows guests on VirtIO SCSI no longer fail with INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE after driver injection, vioscsi gets its own bus type and the device ids it really has and the drivers go into the control set Windows boots from (#823); an Entra sign-in no longer fails with HTTP 500 when a group has no display name (#962); config drift no longer reports an offline node's objects as removed and names the outage once (#968), and a read that failed is no longer taken as a removal; reports load a whole week for Last Week, keep the newest snapshot of a window and size the storage column by the longest node name (#963), with report times in browser time; container migration with a target storage (#808); V2P disks on block storage are allocated as raw on Proxmox 9 (#816); the SMBIOS auto-configurator no longer rewrites a running VM on every cycle (#943) or fills the journal (#969); snapshot times read the same on every page, in browser time and the user's 12h/24h setting (#939); rolling updates on XCP-ng no longer stop at the first node (a 1.2.0 regression); the container dialog lists container templates again, and XCP-ng's from-template path its templates (a 1.2.0 regression); pool grants on LDAP and OIDC groups reach the user, also when typed as a bare group name (#940); a slow answer no longer overwrites the detail view of the next object opened (#828); the client portal's SSO button, the close buttons of three dialogs and Back to Login on the 2FA screen work (#810); the restart button, an update and a rollback restart PegaProx in place instead of stopping it under the Debian package's unit; Unlock all for IPs and users actually unlocks, and the security panel and the support bundle count active sessions; an ESXi host registered for migrations no longer breaks the cluster list; XCP-ng keeps one session per pool; the Cloud skin can be set as the default theme; and a node's management address is found without knocking on the SSH port of a cluster with SSH switched off. KNOWN ISSUE: the experimental Snapshot-Iterative ESXi migration mode can report success with missing or wrong data on the target; use Live Clone or Live Mirror for guests whose data matters. Thanks to everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚
prev_changelog: PegaProx 1.2.0 - a security release built on a full AI-assisted penetration test of the whole codebase, plus the tenant work that was queued behind it. SECURITY: 558 findings were triaged, every critical and high one verified against the code by hand before anything was changed, and the ones that were real were fixed with a regression test and a counter-proof apiece. One class accounted for most of them: a store that fails to load answers with an empty result, and empty was being read as the permissive answer - a tenant table that could not be read handed out every cluster, an unreadable ACL store stopped confining anybody, an unreadable schedule table let a write begin with a DELETE, and a failed settings read bound the syslog receiver's unauthenticated port on an instance that had switched it off. Those now refuse rather than guess. Log injection is neutralised at the sink instead of at seventy-five call sites, so a name carrying escape sequences can no longer repaint an operator's terminal; URLs written into logs have their credentials stripped, which matters because for a webhook the URL is the credential. SDN object ids are validated before they are used as a path segment, where '..' reached a neighbouring API object. The OIDC discovery address is pinned to the address it resolved to, and a group mapping that matches only on display name now says so. LDAP warns when neither TLS nor STARTTLS is configured - the warning used to sit inside the TLS branch, so the one setup that needed it was the one that stayed quiet. Lists that arrive in a request body are bounded, rate limiters can no longer be grown without bound by the thing they limit, and a managed node can no longer hand us output until we run out of memory. The second-factor probe fails closed on both the login and the re-authentication path, so a database hiccup no longer waves a key-only account through. BEHAVIOUR CHANGES: sixteen of them, several of which take something away from an existing setup - a node reboot now requires the node.reboot permission that was defined but never enforced, alert channels need admin.settings to change, PBS resource-wide operations require every linked cluster, ESXi delete and rename moved from vmware.vm.power to vmware.vm.manage, and a pool grant no longer opens an ESXi server. Please read the release notes before updating a multi-tenant install. TENANTS: a per-tenant disk ceiling, a per-tenant VMID slice that restore and template deployment both respect, the tenant list behind them, and self-service container creation serialised per tenant so two requests can no longer clear the same quota check. CI: the APT repository workflow can no longer be dispatched from an arbitrary branch to reach the signing key, the release version is validated before it reaches a shell, and build jobs no longer carry a token that can write to the repository. FIXES: ESXi to Proxmox migration never got past VMID allocation and had not worked since 0.9.2; drift events never reached the configured webhook channels (#815); a failed schedule read could rewrite the whole table; SQLCipher connections raised exceptions two handlers were not catching (#822); the V2P path asked a Proxmox node for a package it does not have (#824); the CVE scan names what failed and measures against the right suite (#825, #827); the console reconnect rides out more than six seconds and mints its ticket on a node that is actually up; a pool grant makes the pool's VMs visible (#793); clusters are labelled by display name everywhere (#787); last_login is recorded for OIDC and Entra logins (#794); node maintenance survives a restart when PVE HA accepted it (#720); the full Proxmox boot-order format is parsed instead of the legacy letters alone (#755); a balancing exclusion is no longer dropped when a cluster enumerates empty; a failed test failover leaves the clone stopped instead of starting it with live NICs; and the status page no longer hands database errors to the browser. Thanks to @karolina-glowinska, @Frisch12, @hugobugomugo, @si458, @mdobprv-lab, @jostrasser, @avsdev-cw, @surreal70 and everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚

PegaProx 1.1.1 — a security and reliability release; every user of 1.1.0 should update. SECURITY: a full audit and pentest pass over the authorization layer closed the recurring class where reaching a cluster was treated as reaching everything on it — per-VM gates now sit on the console, termproxy, PBS, node task-log, search, tag and report paths, and pool- and ACL-scoped accounts stay inside their scope on every one of them. Live streams re-check the account behind them on their own clock and a single account can no longer hold unbounded SSE streams open. Several separately reported issues are fixed and will be described in their own advisories. Encryption-key rotation was rebuilt after it was found to commit re-encrypted rows before the new key reached disk, to miss the PBS, ESXi and VAPID secrets and clusters.ha_settings, and to leave the audit trail reading as tampered. STABILITY: a clean systemd stop that also takes the console subprocess with it (#780, #784); request-pool slots are reclaimed from idle keep-alive connections instead of starving the server (#777); an idle tab dropped from about four REST calls a second to well under one (#782); a same-named cluster no longer steals another's log handler (#783). CONSOLE: pointer latency cut by roughly an order of magnitude at a realistic event rate, the connection-pool churn behind the intermittent drops removed, and the estate-wide IP sweep given its own share of the budget so opening a console does not queue behind it (#713). FEATURES: a VM console can be opened in its own browser window and several watched side by side (#767). The interface now carries its copyright, license and source references on every screen, with the full notice under Settings > About. FIXES: node shell over IPv6 (#778); deleting a cluster purges every table keyed by it (#779); pool assignment gated on pool.assign rather than admin.users (#766); three XCP-ng and ESXi endpoints that raised instead of answering (#781); container create and destroy in the client portal (#765); cluster settings surviving a reconfigure (#762); Corporate ESXi table headers (#753); the compliance dashboard now says why a node check could not run instead of showing 'err 502' (#717); cross-cluster migration fingerprint case (#733); V2P disk copy reporting success after a failure, and an ESXi password left world-readable. Thanks to @Frisch12, @zobsg, @Panxatony, @mikelawson68, @daglimmer, @cybrwerk, @grobe0ba, @hugobugomugo, @mdobprv-lab, @si458 and everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚

PegaProx 1.1.0 — a security-hardening + reliability release. SECURITY: a full Aikido AI-pentest re-triage closed 15 confirmed BOLA / IDOR / token-scope findings — a tenant-custom-role API token now keeps its role name so its cluster scope resolves correctly (it can no longer fall back to 'all clusters'); the auto-balance worker, cluster VM inventory and PBS auto-attach can no longer be reached through a pool / ACL fallback on a cluster the tenant doesn't own; and the live 'resources' SSE stream is scoped to each client's per-VM ACLs (#736). ROLLING UPDATES: evacuation no longer false-fails on 'VM is locked (migrate)' when a guest is already migrating (#647); a benign Ceph HEALTH_WARN (slow BlueStore ops) no longer burns the full 120 s wait (#747); a node that doesn't need a reboot is no longer announced as rebooting, and soft maintenance now survives a PegaProx restart (#715, #720). MIGRATION: ESXi→Proxmox with non-krbd Ceph RBD targets maps librbd URIs to a block device and routes the EFI fallback through them (#722); local snapshot-replicas preserve the source MAC / hostname (#646). CONSOLE: the PVE VNC leg serialises SSL access to stop intermittent disconnects (#713) and the noVNC proxy works under gevent on Python ≥ 3.13 (#740). FEATURES: a usable phone layout with an off-canvas sidebar drawer (#189); re-pin SSH host keys after a node's key changes, e.g. post-CIS-hardening (#717); an optional node FQDN suffix for 'Open in Proxmox' links (#689); reversible umask-027 + lockout warnings on the sshd-hardening controls (#16745). FIXES: WebAuthn / passkey-only accounts can log in (#746); PBS 'passed' disks no longer show red and the overview stopped-VM count uses the explicit stopped status (#751, #749); Corporate light / dark theme handling (#742); iLO 4 stale SEL assertions no longer latch a node Critical (#714); ACME honours the private-CA opt-in and writes issued certs where the TLS listener serves them (#730, #725). LANGUAGES: a new Polish translation (#737) and a backfill of every language to full English parity (de / zh / fr / es / pt / ko / it). QUALITY: 662 automated tests run on every PR, and contributions now carry a PR template + AI-review bar. Thanks to @mikelawson68, @cklabautermann, @Frisch12, @mluenzer, @robertdahlem, @hugobugomugo, @mdobprv-lab and everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚

PegaProx 1.0.2 — a security + maintenance release. SECURITY: closes a per-VM / console access-control bypass where a Client-Portal user scoped to specific VMs could reach any VM on a tenant-owned cluster (assigned a CVE; reported by Jörg Morasch / SYMPLASSON); a broad follow-up audit closed the same object-level authorization gap across bulk + cross-cluster migrate, PBS restore / protect / notes / prune, migration history and the HA plugin, and closed tenant-delegate privilege-escalation paths (a delegate can no longer grant permissions it doesn't hold, reset a higher-privileged peer's password / 2FA, or keep console access after being disabled); and a DNS-rebinding SSRF-guard bypass is closed by pinning the validated IP for outbound requests (GHSA-hmcf-9q7f-vx35; reported by senti-man). AUTH: OIDC login no longer races itself to a logout mid-callback in Firefox (#681), and OIDC group-to-role mappings apply custom roles (#682). FIXES: adding a Proxmox cluster whose account has 2FA now shows a clear, localized message — add with an API token or temporarily disable 2FA — instead of a silent connected-then-offline (#683); the PBS disk table shows SMART health for HDDs without a wearout value (#690); the snapshot overview gained multi-select + bulk delete (#696); EFI and TPM disks accept a raw / qcow2 format (#678); the VM/CT config modal no longer reload-loops (#698) and the backup-verification modal no longer overlaps the PBS UI (#701). FEATURES: rolling updates reboot a node only when needrestart reports a required restart (#694, PR by @gyptazy); an internal / private ACME CA is supported opt-in (#685); a first-class Cloudflare DNS-01 provider was added (#687, thanks @brngates98); hardware-health rollups use live sensor / SEL state and name the contributor (#686); the prebuilt VM / LXC appliances ship sshpass so password-auth SSH works out of the box (#688); and self-update is install-method aware (apt / docker / source). QUALITY: 555 automated tests (authz, integration, SSRF, SSL-bootstrap, hardware, i18n) run on every PR; the whole branch was re-audited and E2E-verified before release. Thanks to Jörg Morasch (SYMPLASSON), senti-man, @gyptazy, @brngates98, @ranydb and everyone who filed, fixed and sponsored.

PegaProx 1.0.1 — a maintenance + feature release on top of 1.0. LANGUAGES: the web UI is now available in Simplified Chinese (#670, thanks @ranydb). CONSOLE: SPICE is offered in every VM console entry point — a downloadable virt-viewer .vv for audio / USB / multi-monitor sessions, alongside the built-in noVNC. SECURITY: another Aikido penetration-test pass closed a set of authorization / IDOR gaps — power- and cost-rate reads are now scoped to the caller's clusters (a scoped API token can no longer enumerate every cluster's rates), the client portal's reboot action is gated on vm.restart instead of vm.start, and further authz / validation / SSRF invariants from batches 1–2 are enforced; the CIS SSH-hardening control no longer disables TCP forwarding (which the built-in VNC console tunnels through), and applied hardening controls are now selectable for rollback. FIXES: adding a disk to a container now targets a container mountpoint (mpN) instead of a QEMU disk key, and never overwrites an occupied slot; a locked VM/CT can be unlocked even on token-authenticated clusters (falls back to qm / pct unlock over SSH); OIDC keeps the full preferred_username instead of truncating at '@' (#486); the storage / snapshot / backup / update action bars follow their backend permissions (#644); scheduled rolling and maintenance updates evacuate local disks by default (#630/#629); node-temperature parsing falls back to plain 'sensors' text when JSON is unavailable (#601); in-band BMC reads fall back key → agent → password so password-only nodes still report hardware health (#609); ESXi / cross-hypervisor migration lists route to their own handlers (#654). PLATFORM: ARM64 / aarch64 build artifacts are now published (#674, gyptazy); cryptography is pinned to 50 and pyOpenSSL to 26.4 to keep the vulnerable 49 line out (#650). QUALITY: 438 automated tests (authorization, integration, SSL-bootstrap, hardware, i18n) run on every PR, and the whole branch was re-audited before release. Thank you to everyone who filed, fixed, translated and sponsored. 💚

PegaProx 1.0 — out of Beta. Everything from the 0.9.x line, hardened and rounded out. SECURITY: a full post-release penetration test closed a BMC-credential exfiltration on the test-BMC endpoint, an ESXi/XCP password ever appearing on a process argv (now fed over stdin/SSHPASS), a BMC/Redfish SSRF oracle, and an SSH-amplification path in the Ceph mirror views; the TLS bootstrap now FAILS CLOSED — if TLS is the intended posture and a usable certificate cannot be loaded or generated, PegaProx refuses to start with an actionable error instead of silently serving plaintext on the TLS port (#633, thanks @SpyrosPsarras). FEATURES: cross-cluster EVPN vNets spanning multiple clusters in the same AS — create / edit / membership / drift-detection + optional reconcile and drift→alert fan-out (#612 cybrwerk); V2P/ESXi migrations gain an opt-in 'wait for confirmation before cutover' gate (#562 ajoergensen); the Top Resources table is now sortable by any column (#621 ccesario); scheduled rolling updates carry a per-schedule reboot/online timeout instead of a fixed 10 minutes (#630). FIXES: nested / hierarchical resource pools now show their members and VM counts (#634 prasannak81); ESXi→PVE migrations of multi-disk VMs to classic LVM no longer abort when a target volume already exists (#636 shepart); XCP-ng→PVE transfers resume by HTTP range instead of failing on a broken pipe (#546). QUALITY: the SSL-bootstrap, authorization and integration test suites continue to run on every PR. Thank you to everyone who filed, fixed and sponsored along the way. 💚

v0.9.15 — a large security-hardening pass (per-VM ACL enforcement, tenant-isolation IDOR/BOLA gates, SSRF guards, RCE-hardening of ISO/template + ESXi-VMDK paths, CSRF/CSP tightening, dependency CVE bumps + AGPL §7(b) attribution), full Cloud-layout parity with Corporate, per-host temperature monitoring with history + alert metric (#601), and scale/perf work (sidebar windowing for 1000+ VMs, TTL caches). Adds a full-stack integration + authz test harness. Community PR #617 snapshot-name validation (thanks @MatrixNeoKozak); welcome TechniData AG Limited (Silver).

v0.9.14.1 — per-disk aio-mode selector in the ESXi→PVE wizard (#598), maintenance-mode RAM pre-flight (#611), Client Portal self-service teardown (#556), OVMF quick-template + reverse-proxy fixes (#607/#614), dependency floors + Site-Recovery log sanitisation; welcome Occentus Network (Platinum)
v0.9.13.3 — flexible snapshot schedules (#586) + replication overview tab (#430) + offline-lag/rolling-update fixes + CIS log-bounds hardening
PBS Reports tab: executive summary, inventory, gap analysis + PDF/PNG export (#273)
Rolling update: optional --with-local-disks evacuation, HA-rerouted migrations no longer false-fail (#330, #340)
Scheduled actions: name and vm_type actually persist now (#337)
Site Recovery: OVS bridges + SDN vnets show up in the network mapping dropdown (#329)
SSH reachability: corosync-VLAN setups now resolve the real mgmt IP for all node ops (#324)
Node Hardening: PDF/PNG export of CIS/Lynis/STIG/PegaProx audit reports
KSM Sharing visible in Node Summary, always shown (matches native PVE UI)
Corporate dashboard: single-node clusters show 'Standalone' badge instead of 'Quorum verloren' (#326)
Disk Create modal: dropdown click no longer dismisses the modal (#323)
breaking_changes: The cloud image catalog no longer has fedora-40 (its image had been gone upstream for a long time), debian-11 and alpine-319 (past end of support). A deploy request with one of those template ids is answered with 400; the catalog now offers fedora-44, debian-12, debian-13 and alpine-324 among others.

Adding storage now requires storage.create; it asked for storage.config before. The Tenant Administrator template does not carry storage.create, so tenant admins and custom roles built on storage.config alone can no longer add storage. Registering an ESXi storage through the generic storage route now requires cluster.admin, like the dedicated ESXi route.

Changing another account's role now requires the caller to hold every permission that account holds, as disabling it or resetting its password already did. A delegate with admin.users can no longer change the role of an account it does not outrank.

An account whose custom role was deleted or cannot be read now has no permissions; it used to fall back to the viewer set. An account in the default tenant whose custom role name is defined in two tenants also resolves to nothing until it is moved into the tenant that was meant.
An admin whom a tenant mapping (an LDAP group mapping, for example) lowers inside a tenant is now held to that lower role there, for the permission check and for the cluster list.

An API token minted with a lower role than its account is now held to that role everywhere: VM ACL and pool grants no longer lift it, its cluster reach follows its owner's tenant, and the lists of scheduled tasks, migration history, affinity rules and alert rules are filtered by the token's role, not by the owner's.

Pool grants on directory groups now take effect. LDAP and OIDC sign-ins store the user's groups, and a grant matches a group's full DN, the bare name of its first part or the last part of an OIDC group path. A user whose group holds a pool grant is now confined to the granted pools on that cluster; before, the grant matched nobody and the user saw whatever the base role allowed. A bare name matches every group of that name in any OU - use the full DN to tell them apart.

Accounts confined to a pool or to VM ACLs on a cluster no longer get whole-cluster data there: the security audit, the drift status, the ESXi endpoints with their guest inventory and ISO and template sync answer 403, and the balancing statistics list only the caller's own guests. The VM ACL list shows only VMs the caller can see, pool permissions answer only for pools the caller can see, and the custom role list shows only the global roles and the caller's own tenant.
Moving a guest into a different pool now requires a managing permission on the pool it is in, not only vm.view on the guest. Adding a guest to the pool it is already in stays allowed.
Replacing an existing second factor now requires the account password: /api/auth/2fa/setup on an account that already has one answers 400 PASSWORD_REQUIRED without it. A first enrolment does not.
Changing the host or the port of a registered ESXi server now requires its password again. Leaving the password out or sending it empty no longer carries the stored one over to the new destination.

?limit= is capped: 5000 on the node syslog and the node task log, 1000 on the node and cluster task lists, the PBS tasks and syslog and the backup verification history. A larger value returns at most the cap. /api/audit is not capped.
Cluster group, drift and schedule routes now answer 404 instead of 403 for an object of another tenant, so the status code no longer tells whether it exists. The refusal is still audited.
Deleting a VM now also removes its VM ACL entries and its favorites. A guest created or restored later on the same VMID starts without them.
Cross-cluster incremental replication resolves a node name only through the cluster's own membership. A job whose node name resolved through DNS alone now fails with a message that names the node.
The client portal creates containers only on a cluster of the customer's tenant, the one its quota counts. A configured target outside that tenant is refused.
A non-admin can no longer clear a PBS server's linked clusters (an empty list makes it reachable by everyone) or link it to a cluster outside their reach; both answer 403.

A cluster's HA settings are written by the HA routes only: the cluster update routes (PUT /api/clusters/<id>, PATCH /api/clusters/<id>/config) and re-configure ignore ha_settings, and a restore keeps the guarded HA switches of the running cluster.

PegaProx node recovery: a two-node or forced-quorum cluster set up from now on is recovered only after a fence per node that was read back (set in the cluster HA settings). Existing setups keep their behaviour behind "unsafe two-node recovery", which lapses when forced quorum is switched off; switching it on again asks for the typed phrase. Recovery also moves a guest only when every volume it starts with is on shared storage: a local disk, an ISO on local storage, a passthrough disk or a host bind mount keep it on the failed node, and so does a config that cannot be read. Detach local ISOs from guests that are expected to fail over.
Only one PegaProx server process may run on a config directory; a second one started next to the service exits with a message.
Bulk migration on an XCP-ng pool now requires xapi.vm.migrate, as a single migration always did. An account without it gets 403 on the bulk route.

Reading a file inside a guest through the guest agent now requires vm.config; it asked for vm.view before. The viewer, tenant viewer, tenant user and VM operator roles, and pool or VM ACL grants without vm.config, get 403.
Taking a guest out of its pool now requires vm.config on the guest.

An admin whom a tenant override lowers now gets 403 on the admin-only routes and on the notification and status page plugin settings, and is confined to the tenant. Only a global admin creates or deletes tenants (403 for admin.tenants held inside a tenant), and a tenant role may not reuse the id of a global or default-tenant role or the other way round (400).
An API token can no longer create API tokens or set up, verify or disable 2FA (403).
With forced 2FA on, a session of an account without a second factor reaches only the 2FA setup, the session check and logout until it enrols (403 MFA_ENROLMENT_REQUIRED).
Sending a test message to an alert channel now requires admin.settings, like changing one.

Accounts confined to a pool or to VM ACLs no longer upload or download ISOs, templates or images and no longer create VMs or containers. A cross-cluster migration onto a cluster the caller is confined on is refused.
An XCP-ng guest now requires its xapi.vm.* permission for clone, delete, snapshot, disk, NIC, CD-ROM and boot order changes and for snapshot policies, as power, config and migrate already did.

Changing a cluster's host, port or fallback hosts, or switching its TLS verification off, now requires the password or token secret again, as PBS and ESXi servers already did. A rename and other edits stay as they were.
Removing the source on a remote migration (Proxmox and cross-cluster) now requires vm.delete, not vm.migrate alone, and confirming an ESXi cutover that removes the source requires vmware.vm.manage.
API clients of the per-node remote migration on an XCP-ng source must send target_cluster (a pool registered in PegaProx) instead of target_endpoint; the request's endpoint is never used.

A clone or a vzdump restore into a new VMID keeps to the tenant's VMID range and, for an account confined to pools or VM ACLs, to nodes of its own guests. Migration and replication land inside the tenant's VMID range, and a VMID sent as a list or object is refused.
ESXi migrations read from the registered ESXi server only. With strict host keys on, the SSH and SSHFS connections the Proxmox node opens follow them as well.
A PBS update that leaves out a field (enabled, fingerprint, ssl_verify, host and others) now keeps the stored value instead of resetting it.
Changing a drift baseline (reset, a scan that seeds it, acknowledging with promote) now requires cluster.config besides admin.audit.

The setup wizard opens only on an install without accounts and without configuration. An install without accounts that still holds clusters, PBS, ESXi or XCP-ng servers, storage clusters, API tokens or security keys answers NO_ACCOUNTS on setup and login; creating config/reopen_setup on the server allows one setup.

The ESXi live clone migration (transfer modes Live Clone and Auto) now carries over what changed on the source after its snapshot: at the switchover it stops the source, waits until ESXi has folded the snapshot back, compares every 256 MiB block of each disk with the copy, transfers and reads back what changed, and only then runs the post-copy steps and starts the target. The switchover therefore takes about one full read of each disk on ESXi instead of a few seconds; for the shortest downtime on large disks use Live Mirror.
